items.title: Ethiopia: Internet disrupted in Tigray amid conflict escalation
items.titleOrig: Ethiopia: Internet disrupted in Tigray amid conflict escalation
items.desc: A web monitor reported an internet disruption in northern Ethiopia amid renewed fighting between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and the federal government.

items.title: How renewed fighting in Tigray could spread across the Horn of Africa
items.titleOrig: How renewed fighting in Tigray could spread across the Horn of Africa
items.desc: The fresh hostilities in Ethiopia's Tigray region come after months of growing animosity between rebel forces and the federal government. Horn of Africa expert Martin Plaut warns of possible regional spillover.

items.title: Nepal's leader says his country is paying the price of climate change
items.titleOrig: Nepal's leader says his country is paying the price of climate change
items.desc: Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah called the devastating Nepal-Tibet floods a "warning to the world" — and questioned if the world had "really heard that warning."

items.title: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
items.titleOrig: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
items.desc: A late Netherlands goal denied Jürgen Klopp a win in his first match as Germany coach. The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss has big ambitions, but the game showed he's going to need more time to achieve them.

items.title: UNGA Day 3: Netanyahu defends Israel as delegates walk out
items.titleOrig: UNGA Day 3: Netanyahu defends Israel as delegates walk out
items.desc: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza the "greatest lie of the century." Many delegates walked out for his General Assembly speech. Mahmoud Abbas also spoke via video.

items.title: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
items.titleOrig: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
items.desc: The era of Russian presidents is coming to an end at the World Chess Federation (FIDE). Two Germans and one Kazakh are up for election. Among the issues at play are money, Kremlin influence, and unanswered questions.

items.title: Ethiopia's military says it killed hundreds of TPLF rebels
items.titleOrig: Ethiopia's military says it killed hundreds of TPLF rebels
items.desc: The TPLF fought against against the Ethiopian military from 2020 to 2022 in a conflict that saw hundreds of thousands of civilians killed. A resumption of fighting has sparked fears of another brutal war.

items.title: After several difficult years, economists now expect German economy to grow
items.titleOrig: After several difficult years, economists now expect German economy to grow
items.desc: Germany's economy is growing again, but recovery remains on shaky ground. High government spending is keeping the economy afloat, while energy prices, a shortage of skilled workers and debt continue to weigh on it.

items.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico regain access to White House
items.titleOrig: CNN, MS NOW, Politico regain access to White House
items.desc: A federal judge has ordered President Trump to restore White House access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico after he banned the media outlets from the premises. Hours later, the media announced they had been granted access.

items.title: Houthi advances in Yemen drive displacement, deepen humanitarian crisis
items.titleOrig: Houthi advances in Yemen drive displacement, deepen humanitarian crisis
items.desc: With more than 132,000 people already displaced by the latest fighting and Houthi territorial gains, Yemen is on the brink of slipping back into a full-fledged humanitarian emergency. DW spoke with people on the ground.

items.title: Nigeria, US agree to boost mining investment on sidelines of UN General Assembly
items.titleOrig: Nigeria, US agree to boost mining investment on sidelines of UN General Assembly
items.desc: On the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Nigeria and the US inked a new mining deal. Nigeria is home to deposits of lithium, gold, tin, gemstones, iron ore and phosphate.

items.title: Extremist parties are thriving ― and that scares people
items.titleOrig: Extremist parties are thriving ― and that scares people
items.desc: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.

items.title: Donald Trump hosts Xi Jinping for state dinner with tech titans.
items.titleOrig: Donald Trump hosts Xi Jinping for state dinner with tech titans.
items.desc: Donald Trump rolled out the red carpet for Chinese leader Xi Jinping, with the two having toasted each other at a lavish state dinner after their summit meeting. America's top tech bosses were also present at the dinner.

items.title: EU to condemn war in Ukraine at G20 even if Putin attends
items.titleOrig: EU to condemn war in Ukraine at G20 even if Putin attends
items.desc: Russian President Vladimir Putin has been invited to the G20 summit in Miami by the United States. Multiple members of the group have called for Moscow's exclusion over its invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
items.titleOrig: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
items.desc: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.
